_meta.description: Reference ranges for liver panel + PBC-specific markers, in SI units as commonly reported on Kazakhstani/Russian lab printouts (not US conventional units). Adult ranges; not age/sex-exhaustive for a v1.
_meta.disclaimer: For patient education only. Not a diagnostic tool. All critical thresholds must trigger escalation to a physician, never an independent conclusion.
_meta.kz_translations_note: Kazakh medical terms provided as a first pass; review with a native-speaking clinician before production use.
sources: AASLD Practice Guidance: Primary Biliary Cholangitis 2018 update
EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines: The diagnosis and management of patients with primary biliary cholangitis 2017
AASLD/EASL cirrhosis and complications guidance (ascites, hepatic encephalopathy)
Standard clinical chemistry reference intervals (adult, SI units) -- most normal_low/normal_high values here, since routine lab reference intervals are physiological, not protocol-specific

Kazakhstan MoH Clinical Protocol for Liver Cirrhosis, 2020 (Protocol No. 135, see rag/corpus/clinical/02_kz_protocol_cirrhosis.md) -- specifically informs the CREATININE critical_high note (HRS Type I criteria) and is the source for the FibroScan F4 cutoff referenced in cirrhosis_note text; the protocol does not publish its own separate numeric reference ranges for routine markers, which is why most other fields cite general clinical chemistry standards instead

markers.cirrhosis_note: In cirrhosis, ALT can be normal or only mildly elevated even with active disease — a normal ALT does not rule out progression. Trend matters more than a single value.
An AST/ALT ratio > 1 is common in cirrhosis regardless of underlying cause.
markers.udca_response_role: Paris-II criterion: AST ≤ 1.5x ULN (≤60 U/L) after 1 year of UDCA therapy indicates adequate biochemical response.

markers.cirrhosis_note: Typically elevated in PBC as a cholestatic marker; tracked alongside ALP rather than in isolation.
The central cholestatic marker for PBC monitoring — sustained elevation reflects ongoing bile-duct injury.
markers.udca_response_role: Paris-II criterion: ALP ≤ 1.5x ULN (≤225 U/L) after 1 year of UDCA therapy indicates adequate biochemical response; failure to reach this threshold should prompt discussion of second-line therapy with the treating physician.

markers.cirrhosis_note: Rising bilirubin is one of the strongest single markers of worsening liver synthetic/excretory function and feeds directly into the MELD-Na score.
markers.udca_response_role: Paris-II criterion: bilirubin within the normal range after 1 year of UDCA therapy is required for an adequate biochemical response.

markers.cirrhosis_note: A rising direct fraction points specifically to cholestasis, consistent with PBC's mechanism.
Reflects the liver's synthetic function; a falling albumin over time (not one low reading) is the meaningful signal and also feeds Child-Pugh scoring.
Interpreted alongside albumin and globulin fraction; a wide albumin-globulin gap can reflect chronic liver disease.
Reflects synthetic (clotting-factor) function; a key input to both MELD-Na and Child-Pugh scores. Rising INR is a serious signal.

Mild-to-moderate thrombocytopenia (roughly 100-150) is EXPECTED in cirrhosis due to portal hypertension and splenic sequestration — this is not, by itself, alarming and should be explained calmly, not flagged as a new problem, unless it falls sharply or crosses the critical threshold.

Renal function is tightly linked to liver disease severity (hepatorenal risk) and is a direct MELD-Na input. The KZ MoH protocol (02_kz_protocol_cirrhosis.md) defines Hepatorenal Syndrome Type I specifically as creatinine doubling to >220 umol/L within 2 weeks -- a dynamic (rate-of-change) criterion the app's trend logic should check in addition to this static critical_high threshold.
Low sodium is common with ascites/diuretic use; a sharp drop below the critical threshold is a recognized marker of decompensation and a direct MELD-Na input.

Used as part of routine HCC (liver cancer) surveillance in cirrhosis patients — a rising value, even within range, should always be routed to escalation for physician review rather than explained away.

The hallmark diagnostic antibody for PBC (positive in ~90-95% of patients). Some Kazakhstani/Russian labs report it quantitatively (IU/mL, e.g. a real observed value of 59 IU/mL against a ~<25 IU/mL negative cutoff) rather than purely qualitatively. Not a monitoring marker for disease activity — once positive, it is tracked for record-keeping/history, not trended for severity like ALP/bilirubin are.

Raw seconds form of the same clotting-time measurement INR is derived from; Kazakhstani coagulation panels typically report PT (sec), PTI (%), and INR together. Prefer the lab's own printed reference range on each report over this default, since reagent-dependent variation is common.
An alternative expression of clotting function alongside PT/INR, commonly reported on KZ/RU lab panels. A falling PTI alongside a rising INR reinforces the same synthetic-function signal.
Part of the routine coagulation panel; reflects a different part of the clotting cascade than PT/INR. Prolongation supports the same synthetic-dysfunction picture.
A clotting factor synthesized by the liver; low fibrinogen supports reduced synthetic function and adds bleeding risk alongside a low platelet count.
Completes the routine KZ/RU coagulation panel alongside PT/PTI/INR/aPTT/fibrinogen; interpreted as part of the same synthetic-function cluster, not in isolation.
Characteristically elevated in PBC; can be tracked as a supportive (not primary) activity marker alongside ALP/bilirubin.
